text.en: In this chapter the river Godavari tells its own story, from the place it begins to the place it meets the sea.

The Godavari begins near Nashik in Maharashtra. It is called Dakshina Ganga because it flows through southern India and is regarded as sacred.
Streams that join a river are its tributaries. Some tributaries receive water only in the rainy season, so they are seasonal rivers.
The river flows through rich forests with tigers, barking deer, the Indian golden gecko and red sandalwood trees.
When the river reaches the sea, it spreads out into many small streams that form a delta. Its freshwater meets the salty sea at the Coringa Mangrove Forests, where the journey ends.
The map shows the course from the mountains down to the sea. A river flows from higher to lower ground following the shape of the land.
Some rivers flow into the Bay of Bengal and some into the Arabian Sea.
Stories of the Godavari come from the Ramayana and the Puranas. People take a dip in its holy waters at Nashik, especially during the Godavari Pushkaram.
Records of India: the Bhupen Hazarika Setu over the Brahmaputra, longer than 9 kilometres, is India's longest river bridge. The Chenab rail bridge is the highest railway arch bridge in the world.

problem.en: Name the parts of a river from start to end.

text.en: The river begins at its source in the hills.
It ends at the mouth and forms a delta at the sea.

prompt.en: Describe a river's journey from mountain to sea.

requiredIdeas.en: Starts as small streams at the source
Forms a delta where it meets the sea

points.en: A river starts at a source and ends at the sea.
Tributaries join it on the way.
A delta forms at the mouth.
